target.title: fix(ios): return promptly from noncooperative timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`AsyncTimeout` used a structured throwing task group. Once the timeout task won, cancelling the operation task did not let the parent return until that child exited. Platform permission, location, or continuation-backed work that ignored cancellation could therefore keep an iOS Gateway invoke visibly stuck past its configured timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper now uses an actor-owned race state and independently owned operation/timeout tasks. The first outcome resumes the caller immediately, cancels the loser cooperatively, and prevents a later completion from resuming the continuation again. Parent-task cancellation resolves the same race with `CancellationError`.

The behavioral boundary is intentional: a non-cooperative platform operation may still finish later, but it can no longer hold the caller past the declared timeout.

## User Impact

Location, permission, and Gateway work protected by `AsyncTimeout` return at their configured timeout even when the underlying platform operation does not promptly observe cancellation.

## Evidence

- Added `AsyncTimeoutTests.timeoutReturnsWhenOperationIgnoresCancellation`, where the operation continues for 100 ms after cancellation while the configured timeout is 10 ms.
- `swiftc -typecheck apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/AsyncTimeout.swift` passed.
- A local `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --jobs 2 --filter AsyncTimeoutTests` compiled `AsyncTimeout.swift` but cannot complete on this host because the package's chat UI needs macOS SwiftUI Preview macros unavailable in Command Line Tools.
- GitHub CI passed the iOS build, macOS Swift, Android test, native i18n, and Node validation lanes for this PR.
- `git diff --check` passed.
